knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The customer buys the outcome, with certainty, such as a structured course and a clear promise about what happens if something goes wrong. Rates and equipment are inputs.
A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford, or it damages the business. The lesson says to promise only the classes, plan and checks you will run.
A measurable claim, such as a percentage improvement, must be backed by evidence that supports it. The lesson says to publish only results you have measured.

practicalCriteria: Applies the step to a real or simulated business decision and records the outcome
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Written output of the step (plan, offer, log or record)
stopWorkCriteria: Not applicable: business guidance; stop if an offer would make an unsubstantiated or misleading claim
